results.description: Every crate directory must contain a Cargo.toml manifest at its root.
A docs/ directory must exist at the workspace root to house project-level.

violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: A docs/ directory must exist at the workspace root to house project-level
documentation.

WHY: Without a dedicated docs/ location, ADRs, design decisions, and onboarding
guides end up scattered in README files, wikis, or not written at all. A
consistent location signals to contributors where to look and where to add.

BEFORE (violating):
  /
    Cargo.toml
    README.md         # sole documentation location  ❌

AFTER (compliant):
  /
    docs/
      1-requirements/
      2-design/
      3-operations/   ✅
    Cargo.toml
    README.md

EDGE CASES:
- doc/ (singular) is also accepted by the rule — either spelling satisfies it.
- The directory must contain at least one file; an empty docs/ directory may
  still trigger downstream content checks.
- This rule applies at the workspace or project root only, not per-crate.

violations.message: Neither doc/ nor docs/ directory exists (recommended for libraries)
violations.fix_hint: Create a docs/ directory for project documentation
violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: Library crates must have a doc/ or docs/ directory for design and API
documentation.

WHY: Rust doc comments (///) generate API docs, but they do not capture design
intent, architectural decisions, or onboarding narrative. A docs/ directory is
the designated home for that longer-form content, making it discoverable to
anyone cloning the repository.

BEFORE (violating):
  scm/my-lib/
    Cargo.toml
    main/src/lib.rs   # no docs/ directory  ❌

AFTER (compliant):
  scm/my-lib/
    Cargo.toml
    docs/
      design.md       ✅
    main/src/lib.rs

EDGE CASES:
- Both doc/ and docs/ satisfy this rule; pick one convention and stick to it
  within the workspace.
- The directory must contain at least one file to avoid triggering content
  checks downstream.

results.description: Library crates should have an examples/ directory demonstrating canonical.

violations.message: examples/ directory does not exist (recommended for libraries)
violations.fix_hint: Create an examples/ directory with usage examples
violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: Library crates should have an examples/ directory demonstrating canonical
usage patterns.

WHY: Examples are the fastest way for consumers to understand how to use the
library. Without them, consumers must read tests or the implementation to
reverse-engineer usage, which is friction that leads to incorrect or
fragile integrations.

BEFORE (violating):
  scm/my-lib/
    Cargo.toml
    main/src/lib.rs   # no examples/  ❌

AFTER (compliant):
  scm/my-lib/
    Cargo.toml
    examples/
      basic.rs        # fn main() showing the golden path  ✅
    main/src/lib.rs

EDGE CASES:
- Add the corresponding [[example]] entries in Cargo.toml so `cargo run --example basic` works.
- This rule is info severity — it does not block CI but is a quality signal.
- Gateway and binary crates are exempt; this is library-focused.

results.description: A bootstrap.sh (or build.sh) must exist at the workspace root to provide.

violations.message: Neither bootstrap.sh nor build.sh exists at project root
violations.fix_hint: Create bootstrap.sh (preferred) or build.sh for project setup
violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: A bootstrap.sh (or build.sh) must exist at the workspace root to provide
a single Unix onboarding command.

WHY: Without it, new contributors must infer setup steps from tribal knowledge
or scattered docs. A single script encodes the canonical first-run procedure
and serves as the living reference for CI as well.

BEFORE (violating):
  /                 # no bootstrap.sh, no build.sh  ❌
    Cargo.toml
    README.md

AFTER (compliant):
  /
    bootstrap.sh    # #!/usr/bin/env bash; set -euo pipefail; cargo build  ✅
    Cargo.toml

EDGE CASES:
- Prefer bootstrap.sh over build.sh — bootstrap connotes environment setup
  (tool installation, env vars) whereas build implies only compilation.
- Do not have both bootstrap.sh AND build.sh simultaneously (see build_bootstrap_exclusivity).
- Make the file executable: chmod +x bootstrap.sh.

results.description: A bootstrap.ps1 (or build.ps1) must exist at the workspace root for.

violations.message: Neither bootstrap.ps1 nor build.ps1 exists at project root
violations.fix_hint: Create bootstrap.ps1 (preferred) or build.ps1 for Windows setup
violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: A bootstrap.ps1 (or build.ps1) must exist at the workspace root for
Windows contributors who use PowerShell.

WHY: Unix shell scripts (.sh) are not executable on Windows by default.
Without a .ps1 counterpart, Windows developers must guess at the equivalent
commands, leading to environment drift between platforms.

BEFORE (violating):
  /
    bootstrap.sh    # Unix only  ❌
    Cargo.toml

AFTER (compliant):
  /
    bootstrap.sh    # Unix  ✅
    bootstrap.ps1   # Windows  ✅
    Cargo.toml

EDGE CASES:
- The .ps1 script should mirror the .sh steps exactly — same tool versions,
  same build flags, same environment variables.
- Add `#Requires -Version 5.1` at the top to enforce minimum PowerShell version.
- Do not have both bootstrap.ps1 AND build.ps1 simultaneously.
